name: FL-06
label: Likely R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with R+14 partisan lean
Incumbent Randy Fine has a massive financial advantage ($1.2M cash, $3.7M outside support)
Democrat Eric Yonce raised only $326K with minimal cash on hand

model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly toward Fine: the district leans Republican by 14 points, he holds incumbency advantages, and he has raised over $4.2M with substantial outside backing versus Yonce's modest $326K. Prediction markets align with this, giving Fine a 94% win probability. No polling or expert ratings exist to suggest an upset is brewing.
model.watch: Any late-breaking scandal or unexpected national wave toward Democrats could tighten this race, but the structural advantages make an upset very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Randy Fine enters this race as a heavy favorite in a district that leans Republican by 14 points. He has raised over $4.2 million and holds more than $1.1 million in cash, supplemented by $3.7 million in outside support. Challenger Eric Yonce has raised about $326,000 with limited cash on hand. Prediction markets give Fine roughly a 94% chance of winning.

No public polling or expert ratings are available for this contest, so the forecast rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and market pricing. A Libertarian and an independent are also on the ballot but appear non-competitive. The race is rated Safe Republican, with modest uncertainty given the absence of polling.
